Create a brooding Gothic cathedral complex on an irregular dark rocky mass in cold blue-gray mist. Pack the central cathedral with connected halls, steep roofs, flying buttresses, arcades, spires, and open belfries. Place smaller monumental chapels, gatehouses, and towers around it, separated by deep chasms and connected to the core by long elevated bridges and narrow causeways. Keep the footprint asymmetrical, with wings radiating outward and broad empty gaps between outer structures. Form stepped cliffs, boulders, and gullies beneath balustraded terraces and pointed arches supported by tall piers. Use weathered brown-gray masonry, dark slate, unlit windows, and sparse warm lamps at bridges and entrances.
